full_judgment:
The appellants as the pre-emptors filed Miscellaneous Case No. 1 of 1992 in the Third Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Chittagong stating, inter alia, that the case land appertaining to RS Plot No. 3797 under RS Khatian No. 3836 belonged to Md. Ismail, grandfather of the appellants, measuring .07 acre of land out of .17 acre. The remaining .10 acre was record in the names of Atarjan and Salima Khatun in equal shares in RS Khatian No. 3838. RS Plot No. 3797 has been recorded in the aforesaid two khatians but the same belonged to one holding. After that, Ismail, the owner of RS Khatian No. 3836, died leaving behind one son and five daughters,- namely, Sajaba, Masma Khatun, Zohura Khatun, Bibi Jan and Masuda Khatun. Bibi Jan died leaving behind two daughters, namely, Jahanara Begum and Ayesha Khatun and sisters, namely, Sajaba, Masma, Zahura and Masuda Khatun. Later, Masuda Khatun died leaving behind husband, Amir Ahmed and other sisters. On 15-11-1977, the appellants and Rahmatullah purchased the shares of other co-sharers of RS Khatian No. 3836 in RS Plot No. 3797. After that, the cousin of the pre-emptors, namely, Ayesha Khatun also transferred her share to the pre-emptors and thus they were co-sharers by inheritance and purchase in the case holding and khatian, Abdun Nabi, grandson of Atarjan, inherited the entire share of Atarjan Abdun Nabi obtained 1ganda of land from RS Khatian No. 3838 but wrongly stated RS Khatian No. 3836 in the registered deed of sale dated 16-9- 1991 showing an inflated amount of Taka 20,000. Pre-emptee Nos. 1 and 2 are strangers to the case land. After that, the pre-emptors collected the certified copy of the deed of sale dated 16-9-1991 and became aware of the trans- action and filed the miscellaneous case for pre- emption. 

 3. The pre-emptees contested the case by filing written objection denying all the material statements made in the application for pre-emption. Their case, in short, is that the case pond of RS Plot No. 3797 comprising 0.17 acre out of which .07 acre was recorded in RS Khatian No. 3836 and the remaining .10 acre in RS Khatian No. 3838 but both the jama and holding are separate. The pre-emptors are co-sharers in RS Khatian No. 3836 but not in RS Khatian No. 3838. Abdun Nabi purchased .09 acre of land of RS Plot No. 3797 under RS Khatian No. 3838 on 7-7-1933 from Solima Bibi, Amena Bibi, Asma Khatun. In the deed of sale, Abdun Nabi was shown to have purchased .07 acre of land of RS Plot No. 3797 under RS Khatian No. 3838. Abdun Nabi by inheritance and purchase got title in .10 acre of land which later devolved upon his heir Mahfuza Khatun. After that, Mahfuza Khatun transferred .20 acre of land from RS Plot No. 3838 for consideration of Taka 20,000 to the pre-emptees by a deed of sale dated 16-9-1991. The pre-emptors were asked to purchase the case property and they offered only Taka 5,000 for which their offer was turned down. The pre-emptees developed the case land by spending huge amount of money. Hence, they prayed for dismissal of the pre-emption case. 

 7. Mr Omar Farook, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the appellants, submits that the High Court Division came to a finding that the pre-emptors are non co-sharers in RS Khatian No. 3838 and that on the contrary they are co-sharers in RS Khatian No. 3836 although the pre-emptors by filling an application for amendment before the appellate Court amended the application for pre- emption stating that they are also co-sharer tenants in RS Khatian No. 3838 and that the High Court Division without taking into consideration that fact delivered the judgment and, as such, the impugned judgment should be set-aside. He further submits that in case of a pre-emption under section 24 of the Non-Agricultural and Tenancy Act if a tenant is co-sharer in the plot he is also treated as a co-sharer in that plot even if the said plot is recorded in more than one khatian. 

 9. Initially, the pre-emptors filed the pre-emption case stating that they are co-sharers of RS Plot No. 3797 appertaining to RS Khatian No. 3836. 

 11. In the case in hand, it appears that in the appellate Court the pre-emptors filed an application under Order VI Rule 17 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for amendment of the application for pre-emption filed under section 24 of the Non-Agricultural and Tenancy Act stating that they are also co-sharer tenants in RS Khatian No. 3838. In support of their contention, they produced a registered deed of sale dated 27-11-1940 to show that their father Md. Younus purchased land from RS Khatian No. 3838 and, as such, they are also co-sharer tenants by inheritance in that khatian. The application for' amendment was allowed by the appellate Court by Order No. 12 dated 3-6-1993. The High Court Division came to a wrong finding that the: pre-emptors are not co-sharers in RS Khatian No. 3838 and, as such, reversed the findings of the appellate Court holding that the pre-emptors are not entitled to pre-empt the case land. By amendment of the application for pre-emption, the pre-emptees could prove that they have got interest in RS Khatian No. 3838. 

 12. In a case of pre-emption filed under section 24, of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act if a co-sharer tenant owns a portion of land in any plot, he is to be. treated as co-sharer in the entire plot even if the land of that plot is recorded in more than one khatian. Therefore, in the event of transfer of a portion of land of that plot appertaining to another khatian a co-sharer tenant can file a pre-emption case under section .24 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act notwithstanding the fact that he does not have any interest in that khatian. The words "one or more co- sharer tenants of such land" occurring in section 24 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act means a co- sharer in the plot not the holding as mentioned in section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. Such being the position of law, the pre-emptors were not even required to file an application for amendment to show that they have also interest in RS Khatian No. 3838. 

 14. Without looking into that legal aspect, the High Court Division came to a finding that the pre-emptors could not prove that they have also interest in RS Khatian No. 3838.
